1 · Overview

What the Federated tab is

The Federated tab is a new top-level tab on the existing Tower module, alongside today's per-HoldCo Tower views. It is the only surface where a viewer can see all three Lakeshore L1 HoldCos (Morgan Street, Roosevelt, Lakefront) in one frame. Everything on the page is one click away from a drill-down into the originating Move, Source event, or CXO bundle.

The mental model is a Datadog monitoring tab, but for a multi-HoldCo portfolio of AI and modernization Moves. Density is high in the rollup zones (Zone A, B, E) and focus mode in detail zones (Zone F capability detail). Charts are single-color line charts on white cards; no gradients, no emoji legends, no animation.

3 · Zone-by-zone full-fidelity spec

Zone A · Portfolio rollup strip

Purpose

The "Datadog top row" for the portfolio. Three cells, one per HoldCo. Each cell answers four questions in under two seconds of scan: which Moves are active, what phase each is in, how much value is at stake, when was the last data update.

Visual mockup data

CellHoldCoMoves shownValue at stakeLast update note

2Roosevelt HoldingsMove 0 Phase 0 (Setup load) · Move 4 (auto-running)$6.4M (share of Move 2 $2.4M + Move 0 projected close accel $1.0M + Move 3 federated platform savings est $3.0M)2026-06-03 23:02 · CIO bundle initial load by Edward Park

Data sources

  • moves table filtered on tenant_id IN (SELECT child_tenant_id FROM tenant_holding_group WHERE holding_group_id = current_holding_group())
  • move_phases for current phase per Move
  • move_value_at_stake view — aggregates business case projected savings + open Source event estimated value attributed to that HoldCo's share
  • cxo_bundle_loads for last-update timestamp (most recent bundle load per HoldCo)

Refresh

Nightly aggregate refresh at 02:00 UTC. Manual "refresh now" affordance in cell overflow menu when a CXO bundle is reloaded mid-day and the L0 viewer wants the latest read before a meeting.

Drill-down

Click any Move pill → navigates to that Move's page (Move 0 canvas, Move 2 cross-HoldCo view, etc.) scoped to that HoldCo. Click the HoldCo name → navigates to that HoldCo's per-HoldCo Tower view (the existing non-federated Tower). Click the value at stake → opens a breakdown popover with the components from the data sources table above; each component links to its originating artifact (Source event, business case, Move).

Empty state

When a HoldCo cell has no loaded bundles: cell renders the HoldCo name + the literal text "CXO bundles not loaded — start with CIO + CFO via Setup loader" with a direct link to /setup/cxo-loader?tenant=<holdco_id>. Value-at-stake shows an em-dash, not $0 — see locked rule "do NOT show zeros as if 0 is real". Moves row shows no pills; renders as faint italic "awaiting bundle load".

Atlas chat affordance

When the sticky bar viewport is over Zone A, the Atlas placeholder rewrites to: "e.g., which HoldCo's Move 0 is furthest along?" or "why is Roosevelt's value at stake lower than Morgan Street's?". Send routes to Atlas with the Zone A data already in the context window.

Zone B · Cross-HoldCo opportunities surfaced this week

Purpose

The "one new thing to consider this morning" surface. AbarVa proactively names opportunities the L0 sponsor would not have surfaced themselves: vendor overlaps detected once enough bundles are loaded, contract renewal calendars that synchronize across HoldCos, capability fork eligibility from one HoldCo to another, risk threshold crossings that recommend an action.

Visual mockup data (5 opportunities, week of 2026-06-02)

  1. Microsoft EA federation · all 3 HoldCos · $9.1M consolidated spend · enterprise rate threshold at $9M+ · Morgan Street EA expires 2026-12-31 · projected savings $1.0-1.4M
  2. Federated Big-4 audit RFP · all 3 HoldCos on KPMG · $5.4M consolidated fees · synchronized 2026-10 renewal window in 18 weeks · projected $0.5-0.8M
  3. Cyber carrier split · 2 of 3 on same carrier · concentration threshold breach 2026-04-22 · two-carrier program recommended · projected $0.3-0.5M plus risk reduction
  4. Capability fork — covenant headroom forecasting · Lakefront Cap 3 production 14 months · Morgan Street eligible to fork post-G4 green
  5. Federated Workday SI partner selection · Roosevelt in flight, Morgan Street Wave 2 queued · 20-30% implementation cost compression

Data sources

  • cross_holdco_opportunities table — populated by the Move 2/3/4 opportunity ranker (Wave 2 Spec L07)
  • Ranker inputs: vendor overlap matrix (CIO + GC bundles) · contract renewal calendar (CFO + GC) · capability marketplace eligibility (CIO + Move 1 production state) · risk threshold breaches (Move 4 monitor)
  • Surface filter: only opportunities new this week or changed this week (e.g., a renewal window just opened, a threshold just breached)

Refresh

Weekly Monday 06:00 UTC ranker run; opportunities marked "new this week" persist through Friday EOD, then archive into the opportunities ledger (accessible via drill-down). Ad-hoc surfacing on threshold breach (Move 4 monitors push directly to this zone within 15 minutes of detection).

Drill-down

"Review" button on each opportunity routes to a structured opportunity page with: the underlying evidence (which bundles + which records sourced the claim), the recommended action (e.g., "spawn Source event L-S02"), the affected HoldCos, the stakeholders that need to consult, the historical pattern reference (corpus pattern ID or similar prior Lakeshore opportunity). From the opportunity page, L0 can directly spawn the Source event (one click — Source module redesign handles the rest) or route to the Move that should pick it up.

Empty state

When fewer than 2 HoldCo CIO+CFO bundles are loaded: zone renders the literal text "Cross-HoldCo opportunities surface when 2 or more HoldCos have completed Wave 1 CXO bundle load. 1 of 3 HoldCos complete." with progress dots. Do not render "0 opportunities" — that implies the ranker ran and found none, which is misleading. When 2+ HoldCos loaded and ranker ran but found no new opportunities this week: zone renders "No new opportunities this week. Last refresh Mon 06:00 UTC. View opportunities ledger →".

Atlas chat affordance

Placeholder rewrites to: "e.g., why is the Microsoft EA opportunity ranked first?" or "what's the latest cyber carrier breach detail?". Atlas can explain the ranker's scoring inputs but will not spawn the Source event — that requires explicit L0 click for audit trail.

Zone C · Federated savings ledger

Purpose

The "savings trending up" credibility surface. Two views: a single-color cumulative line chart (projected vs realized over 12 months rolling) and a per-source table breaking out each savings stream with its current status. The rule: realized = money the corpus or evidence chain can defend as actually saved or unlocked. If we cannot defend it, it is not in realized.

Visual mockup chart

Two lines on a single chart frame. Projected (solid accent blue) ramps from $0.18M in July to $4.10M by May. Realized (dashed ink-soft) ramps from $0.18M in July (Lakefront baseline) to $1.42M in May. The realized line lags by 6-10 percentage points across the year — visually communicating "in flight, on track, not pre-counted".

Data sources

  • savings_ledger_entries — one row per source × month, with projected + realized columns
  • business_cases — provides projected curve for each Source event and Move
  • evidence_chains — provides realized claim provenance (every dollar realized has a chain back to a controllable artifact: closed contract, measured KPI delta, etc.)
  • source_events + moves for cross-reference

Refresh

Nightly. Realized claims gated by evidence chain freshness — if the evidence chain has not been validated in 90+ days, the realized claim is automatically marked "stale" and excluded from the YTD total until re-validated.

Drill-down

Click any row in the table → opens that source's full ledger view: month-by-month projected and realized, the underlying business case, the evidence chain for every dollar claimed realized. Click the chart → opens a stacked-by-source variant of the same chart. Hover over a chart point → tooltip with projected vs realized for that month.

Empty state

When no business cases exist and no realized claims chained: zone renders "Savings ledger populates as Move business cases are approved and realized milestones are evidenced. 0 business cases approved across the portfolio." Do not show a $0 line on the chart — render the chart placeholder with a faint dashed axis only. When projected exists but no realized yet: render projected line only, with the literal note "No realized claims yet — ledger reflects projected only."

Atlas chat affordance

Placeholder rewrites to: "e.g., why did the realized line dip in Feb?" or "what's the evidence for L-S01's $0.62M realized?". Atlas can name the evidence chain in detail (the chain itself is L0-readable; the underlying transaction grain may require a HoldCo grant for full read).

Zone D · Risk concentration trend

Purpose

The "one risk to monitor" surface. Four concentration measures plotted as time series over 6 months: auditor concentration, cyber carrier concentration, banking concentration, single-vendor concentration. Each measure has an amber threshold (dashed horizontal) and a red threshold. Trend deltas (+/- pp week over week) tell the L0 viewer not just where things are, but where they are going.

Visual mockup chart

Four lines on a single chart frame, single-color per line (red, amber, green, blue — matching status semantics). Dashed amber threshold line at 60%. Auditor trend flat at 100% (red). Cyber carrier trend climbed from 50% to 67% Apr-May (amber breach). Banking trend slowly improving from 35% to 32% (green). Single-vendor cyber trend climbing from 65% to 78% (amber, watch).

Data sources

  • risk_concentration_snapshots — daily snapshot per HoldCo per concentration measure
  • Auditor concentration: cfo_bundle.audit_firms + gc_bundle.advisor_engagements
  • Cyber carrier concentration: cfo_bundle.insurance_carriers filtered category = cyber
  • Banking concentration: cfo_bundle.banking_relationships · normalized count + concentration index (HHI-style)

Refresh

Nightly snapshot. Threshold breach detection runs at end of snapshot job; if breached, Move 4 ad-hoc event spawns within 15 minutes and Zone B opportunity surfaces same day.

Drill-down

Click a risk row → opens that risk's full Move 4 page: which HoldCos contribute, what the concentration index is per HoldCo, what mitigation options exist (with corpus references), what historic concentration looked like (12-month rolling), and the recommended action with stakeholders. Click the chart → opens a per-measure detail with HoldCo-level decomposition.

Empty state

When fewer than 2 HoldCo bundles are loaded for a category (e.g., GC bundles not yet loaded for auditor risk): that row renders "Insufficient bundle coverage — auditor risk needs GC bundle from at least 2 HoldCos. 1 of 3 loaded." Do not render a 0% or flat line if the data is insufficient — render the chart line as dashed with the literal annotation "data incomplete."

Atlas chat affordance

Placeholder rewrites to: "e.g., what's the impact if KPMG raises rates 10%?" or "how concentrated is Roosevelt's vendor base vs Lakefront's?". Atlas can run cross-HoldCo concentration counterfactuals at the aggregate level (e.g., "if we split cyber carrier, concentration drops to 33%"); concentration-of-grain transaction-level questions require HoldCo grant.

Zone F · Capability marketplace

Purpose

Focus-mode zone. Production AI workloads cataloged by HoldCo with reuse metadata. Cards (not table) because each capability deserves a moment of attention — this is where the L0 OP-Tech (Marcus Rhee) spends most reading time once steady state is reached. The L0 viewer's job here is to identify capabilities ready to fork and to nominate eligible HoldCos.

Visual mockup data (3 cards, all Lakefront-originated)

  1. 12-week forward cash forecast · Lakefront · 18 months in production · Prophet ensemble · daily refresh. Realized: variance 8% → 2.4%; $1.2M working capital unlock. Reusability: high.
  2. Payment anomaly + BEC fraud detection · Lakefront · 14 months · gradient-boosted + LLM context · realtime. Realized: FP rate <2%; 2 BEC attempts intercepted YTD. Reusability: high.
  3. Covenant headroom forecasting · Lakefront · 14 months · scenario-tree · weekly refresh. Realized: 2 advance warnings before quarterly cert. Reusability: medium.

Eligibility callout at bottom: "Morgan Street CIO (Daniel Okonkwo) has expressed interest in capabilities 1 and 3. Eligibility check: G1-G4 green required for Cap 1; covenant agreement load required for Cap 3."

Data sources

  • capability_marketplace table — one row per production AI workload; populated by Move 1 / Move 3 production-state tracking
  • Required workload metadata: business problem · model type · data dependencies · realized impact (with evidence chain) · reusability rating (auto-derived from data dependency complexity + tuning requirements)
  • Eligibility check: capability_eligibility_view — joins capability prerequisites against each HoldCo's current Move state
  • Interest signals: capability_fork_requests — populated when HoldCo CIO clicks "express interest" in their own Tower view

Refresh

On-demand when CIO bundle changes or Move 1 production state changes. Manual "refresh" affordance in zone overflow for L0 viewer. Eligibility check runs nightly with the rest of the Tower aggregates.

Drill-down

Click a capability card → opens that capability's full marketplace detail: model architecture summary, prerequisites in plain language, fork process (estimated effort, blockers, stakeholders), evidence chain for the realized impact claim, the originating HoldCo's contact for technical handoff. "Request fork" button → routes to the originating HoldCo's CIO for grant + spawns a Move 1 instance at the requesting HoldCo pre-filled with the source capability.

Empty state

When no production AI workloads exist across the portfolio: zone renders "Capability marketplace populates as Move 1 capabilities reach production. 0 production capabilities across the portfolio." Below that, a faint "Lakefront's Move 1 is the demo seed; capabilities surface here once Move 1 ships Phase 5 mobilization at Lakefront." Do not render fake placeholder cards.

Atlas chat affordance

Placeholder rewrites to: "e.g., what would it take for Morgan Street to deploy Cap 1?" or "which capabilities have Roosevelt eligibility?". Atlas can describe eligibility logic and surface prerequisite gaps; it cannot grant the fork (requires explicit originator CIO click for audit trail).

4 · Information density discipline

Density varies by mental task. The rollup zones (A, B, E) are scan-mode and high density — the viewer is checking for "anything new, anything wrong, anything to dive into". The detail zones (Zone F capability detail) are read-mode and focus mode — the viewer is committing attention to one capability, one fork decision.

ZoneModeDensity targetPattern
Top status stripsquint4 numbers, maxWide column, large serif numerals, single delta caption
Zone A rollupscan3 cells × 4 facts each = 12 facts in 200px heightCompact pill rows, value-at-stake as serif headline per cell, faint updated timestamp
Zone B opportunitiesscan5 rows × 5 fields each visible without scrollingRow grid, single-line title with two-line description, right-aligned value in serif
Zone C savings ledgerscan + readChart + 7-row tableSingle-color line chart on white card, table beneath, no nested tables
Zone D risk concentrationscanChart + 4-row table4-line single-chart, threshold dashed reference line, table with delta column
Zone E CXO performancescan3 × 3 KPI grid + 5-column secondary tableGrid cells with KPI in serif and benchmark below; secondary table for less-frequent KPIs
Zone F capability marketplaceread / focus3 cards stacked, full-width eachCard layout; title in serif; impact paragraph; reusability pills; single CTA per card

Per the "one dark moment" rule note in the brief: this page is portfolio monitoring, not decision-rendering, so the dark moment rule does not apply. Every zone is allowed to be its own micro-moment of attention.

Honesty discipline"I need X to answer this" when bundle missingSame · plus "this HoldCo has not granted transaction-grain read; I can show aggregate only"

How the sticky ask bar works

The Atlas ask bar is sticky to the bottom of the viewport when the user scrolls past Zone A. It auto-grows on text input (1 line → up to 6 lines). Enter submits; Shift-Enter is line break. Spellcheck enabled. The placeholder text rewrites contextually based on which zone is centered in the viewport (zones B-F each have a dedicated example query).

What Atlas can answer

  • "Why is the Microsoft EA opportunity ranked first?" → ranker scoring inputs + corpus reference for the enterprise-rate threshold
  • "What's the evidence for L-S01's $0.62M realized?" → evidence chain summary (banking contracts closed, fee reduction baseline, attribution method)
  • "Which HoldCo is most exposed if KPMG raises rates 10%?" → cross-HoldCo aggregate counterfactual on auditor concentration
  • "What would it take for Morgan Street to deploy Cap 1?" → prerequisite chain + estimated effort + Lakefront contact for handoff

What Atlas refuses (and how it refuses)

  • "Show me Roosevelt's underlying bank-by-bank fee detail" → "Roosevelt has not granted transaction-grain banking detail to the federated view. I can show their aggregate banking concentration (32% HHI) but not per-bank. To get per-bank detail, request grant from Edward Park (Roosevelt CIO) or Priya Naidu (Roosevelt CFO). I can draft the grant request if you'd like."
  • "Spawn the federated audit Source event right now" → "Source spawns from this surface require explicit L0 click for audit trail. I've prepared the spawn payload (3 incumbent contracts, scope standardization, fee-compression target). The 'review' button on opportunity 02 in Zone B will open the spawn dialog."
  • "What's the EBITDA per PortCo at Roosevelt?" → "Aggregate read does not include per-PortCo EBITDA. Roosevelt's CFO bundle aggregates at the HoldCo level. Request grant from Priya Naidu for the per-PortCo view, or ask Atlas about the consolidated $182M EBITDA figure."

Atlas memory + context window

Atlas sessions are scoped to the federated tab visit. Long-term memory of L0 preferences (e.g., "Anya prefers concentration trends weekly") is held in a small per-L0-viewer preference store; conversation transcripts are persisted as audit artifacts and visible in Setup / Admin under the L0 audit trail.

6 · Tenancy + visibility

What L0 sees

  • All six zones at full fidelity
  • Per-HoldCo aggregates in Zone A (active Moves, phases, value at stake, last update)
  • All cross-HoldCo opportunities in Zone B regardless of which HoldCos are affected
  • Federated savings ledger (Zone C) summing across all HoldCos and Source events
  • Risk concentration trend (Zone D) with all four measures across all HoldCos
  • CXO performance KPIs (Zone E) with HoldCo names visible
  • Capability marketplace (Zone F) with full reusability and originator information

What an L1 HoldCo CXO sees on the same page

  • Zone A: own HoldCo cell is pinned to the left with a "you" badge; sibling HoldCo cells are present but show aggregate-only summaries (no value-at-stake per sibling, only "Moves in flight: N" and "concentration risk delta: +/− X")
  • Zone B: opportunities affecting own HoldCo are surfaced fully; opportunities that do not affect own HoldCo are visible as compact rows ("Federated audit RFP — does not affect your HoldCo")
  • Zone C: own HoldCo's realized + projected pulled out as a separate line; portfolio total shown for context but not broken out per sibling
  • Zone D: concentration measures show portfolio aggregate; own HoldCo's contribution is highlighted; sibling contributions are anonymized ("HoldCo B: 4 banks", not "Roosevelt: 4 banks")
  • Zone E: own HoldCo's row at full fidelity; sibling rows show anonymized peer benchmarks ("Peer 1: 2.8% IT spend / rev")
  • Zone F: marketplace shows all capabilities; fork eligibility shows for own HoldCo only

Substrate enforcement

The visibility rules above are enforced at the data layer via the holding-group tenancy substrate (Wave 1 Spec L01). Server components query through tenant-aware view layers that resolve own-vs-sibling based on the viewer's tenant membership and role. No client-side filtering is trusted — the API only returns what the viewer is allowed to see.

7 · Squint test

The "if a CFO blurs the page 50%, what survives" check, per zone.

Top strip
5 of 5 · $32.9M · $1.42M · 3 — four serif numerals in a row
The viewer sees portfolio health in five seconds: all Moves on track, addressable spend large, realized trending up, three concentration flags to watch. If any number is wrong, the morning has a different shape.
Zone A
Three columns, three large serif $11.2M / $6.4M / $2.1M values stacked vertically per cell
The viewer sees relative HoldCo weight in three seconds. Morgan Street is the heavyweight, Lakefront is the established baseline, Roosevelt is the newer addition.
Zone B
Five horizontal rows · right-aligned serif values · "review" buttons in a column
The viewer sees five new opportunities and their respective dollar magnitudes. One should be the most interesting. The "review" column is the call-to-action lane.
Zone C
One chart · two lines · the solid (projected) above the dashed (realized) but both trending up
The viewer sees savings credibility: realized is real but lags projected, and the gap is consistent. No suspicious surge, no flat dashed line.
Zone D
One chart · four lines · one (auditor) flat at red, one (cyber) climbing into amber, others stable
The viewer sees one risk trend escalating (cyber carrier) and the rest stable. That escalation is the conversation to have today.
Zone E
Three-row grid · the third row (Lakefront) clearly outscoring the others on AI maturity
The viewer sees that the portfolio has one mature HoldCo and two earlier-stage HoldCos. That's the federation arbitrage opportunity.
Zone F
Three vertical cards · each with one serif title · "request fork" buttons aligned right
The viewer sees three forkable capabilities and a clear action affordance per card. Focus mode — no scan, just commit.

8 · Action affordances

What does L0 click to do the four common actions?

ActionWhere to clickWhat happens
(a) Drill into a HoldCoHoldCo name in Zone A cell · or HoldCo tab in the Tower top tab rowNavigates to that HoldCo's per-HoldCo Tower view (existing non-federated Tower). L0 retains full read of own portfolio at that level.
(b) Launch a Move 2/3/4 event"Review" on Zone B opportunity · or "Spawn Move event" from a Zone D risk rowOpens the spawn dialog with pre-filled facts (the opportunity ranker's outputs become the spawn payload). One additional click to confirm. The Move shows up in Zone A within minutes of confirmation.
(c) Approve a Source spawn"Review" on a Zone B opportunity tagged "Source spawn ready" · or directly from the originating Move page when a Source event has been pre-stagedOpens the Source spawn dialog (Source module redesign). The spawn is gated on L0 sponsor signature for federated events (Move 2/3/4); HoldCo-scoped Source events (Move 0/1) are gated on the HoldCo CXO instead and surface to L0 only as informational.
(d) Ask Atlas a questionSticky Atlas ask bar at the bottom of the viewportAtlas responds in a side panel that does not collapse the underlying zone. Responses are persisted as audit artifacts for L0 reference.
Bonus · request capability fork"Request fork" on a Zone F capability cardRoutes to originator HoldCo CIO (Yuki Ono at Lakefront, in most cases) for grant. On grant, spawns a Move 1 instance at the requesting HoldCo with pre-filled capability metadata.
Bonus · navigate to Atlas-only logAccount menu · "L0 audit trail"Setup / Admin audit view filtered to L0 viewer's session history + Atlas conversation transcripts.

10 · Acceptance criteria

The build is acceptance-ready when the following are true:

  1. An L0 sponsor logs in and lands on /tower/federated within one click of the home shell.
  2. The top status strip renders four numerals in serif, all derived from real (or seeded for demo) data with delta annotations.
  3. Zone A shows three HoldCo cells with the correct active Moves, current phases, value-at-stake numerals in serif, and last-update timestamps.
  4. Zone B renders the five opportunities surfaced this week from the ranker; each "review" routes to a structured opportunity page; spawning a Source event from an opportunity creates a valid pre-filled spawn payload that the Source module redesign accepts unchanged.
  5. Zone C renders the projected and realized cumulative lines with consistent y-axis; the realized line never exceeds the projected line; the source table accurately reflects evidence chain freshness (stale items excluded from YTD totals).
  6. Zone D renders four concentration time series with the correct thresholds visible; threshold breach detection populates Zone B opportunities and Move 4 ad-hoc events within 15 minutes of breach.
  7. Zone E renders the 3 × 3 grid plus the modernization-debt secondary table; each KPI cell links to its underlying CXO bundle detail.
  8. Zone F renders the three Lakefront capabilities with reusability and eligibility metadata; "request fork" routes to the originator CIO.
  9. The Atlas ask bar is sticky, auto-grows, context-aware per zone, and routes through the AgentContextBroker (no direct broker imports).
  10. HoldCo CXOs visiting the same page see the own-HoldCo-prominent / peer-anonymized variant per the tenancy + visibility section.
  11. Empty states render specific missing-input messaging — never "0" or "—" implying real-zero — per the locked rule.
  12. All API routes are gated on holding_group_id membership + L0 sponsor role at server entry; no client-side filter is relied upon for tenancy.
  13. The page passes the squint test: a CFO blurs the page 50%, the dominant elements per zone match the table in section 7.

11 · Open design questions parked for future waves

  • Configurable zone order. Different L0 viewers (Op-Tech vs Op-Finance) may want a different default zone order. Parked for Wave 4 — for now, the canonical order in this spec is what ships.
  • Annotations layer on charts. "Threshold breach on 2026-04-22" as a chart annotation is desirable but parked until the charting library decision is made. Wave 4.
  • Exportable views. "Export this page as a board memo PDF" is a likely IC ask. Parked for Wave 4; coordinate with the deliverables library pattern in Setup.
  • Push notification on threshold breach. L0 sponsors may want a daily digest or breach-only push. Parked for Wave 4; depends on the notification substrate.
  • Per-PortCo drill-through. Currently the page goes HoldCo → Tower; a future iteration may surface PortCo-level callouts when a single PortCo materially drives a HoldCo metric (e.g., the legacy specialty mfg PortCo dragging Morgan Street's modernization debt). Parked for Wave 4+.
